outcome: LAUNCHED AND FAILED BEFORE SCIENCE, after materializing ALL FIVE arms at their recorded identities and training the first probe. No probe was scored; no ranking and no selection exist.
classification: PRE-SCIENCE ENGINEERING ABORT (P12.1): the shared engine probe could not import its own dependency, so no generation protocol could be attested and the driver refused to score -- which is the admission gate behaving exactly as designed. NOT a DIGEST_MISMATCH and not a scientific finding.

root_cause.why: the information-architecture migration moved the evaluator to scripts/shared/evaluation/ and rewrote the probe's import to `shared.evaluation.uncapped_eval` -- which needs `scripts` on sys.path, because `shared` is a package under it -- but left the probe's own insert naming `scripts/evaluation`, which has not existed since. The probe could not import on ANY machine.
root_cause.why_no_gate_caught_it: every phase that runs the probe (C1, C3, A3) closed before the migration, and it is only ever executed as a bare subprocess on a pod. A driver sets sys.path IN PROCESS, which puts nothing in os.environ, so its subprocesses inherit no PYTHONPATH and must be self-sufficient.

repair: the probe inserts `scripts` rather than `scripts/evaluation`. tests/integration/test_pod_script_imports_resolve.py pins the CLASS: for every script a driver spawns bare, each module-level first-party import must resolve under the paths that script sets for ITSELF, with no ambient PYTHONPATH -- and the complementary contract is asserted too, that the runner supplies PYTHONPATH for the collector and watchdog, which deliberately set none. A repo-wide sweep found 127 stale path inserts; all but this one are no-ops because the module resolves through another entry the script also adds, and they are left for a maintenance round rather than edited during a live experiment.

The teardown gate refused until that was true, then allowed. This is exactly the state-2 window the third review required be covered, and it was covered by the poll-loop preservation rather than at closeout.

the_preserved_probe.will_the_next_attempt_restore_it: NO, and the reason is transport cost
the_preserved_probe._why_not: restoring means UPLOADING 2.38 GiB from this host at a measured ~0.72 MB/s -- about 53 minutes of billing pod time -- against ~61 minutes to retrain the same frozen unit at the same arm, seed and recipe. The saving is ~8 minutes and the restore path has never executed on a pod, so it would be a new risk surface on a paid session for no material gain. P8.4's own framing is that unnecessary data movement is an engineering defect and that $0 of GPU is not free. The copy is KEPT as evidence that the mechanism works and as insurance if a later attempt loses the same unit at greater cost.
